pr_title: [Fixes #19666] [Components] Improve reliability of component quarantined tests (take 2)
pr_body:
* Tries to increase the reliability of the tests by:
  * Trying to ensure that the server is up and running before connecting.
  * Retrying a connection attempt multiple times.
pr_comments: Do you have any failures I can take a quick look at?

I believe the other potential cause is the server taking longer to start on the CI, I ran the tests locally on my box 200+ times in a loop and wasn't able to repro it.

One interesting thing to note is that when these tests are quarantined, they don't seem to fail anymore. But when you accidentally un-quarantined them last week they failed pretty quickly.

Also, it would be nice if you could enable timestamps in the server logs. Only the client logs have timestamps currently.

> One interesting thing to note is that when these tests are quarantined, they don't seem to fail anymore. But when you accidentally un-quarantined them last week they failed pretty quickly.

Bad luck? Karma? Destiny? Murphy's law?

> Also, it would be nice if you could enable timestamps in the server logs. Only the client logs have timestamps currently.

No idea how to enable that, do you have any thoughts? If it's simple I'm happy to do it.

I'm thinking more like machine resource starvation from the parallel test runs.

> No idea how to enable that, do you have any thoughts?

Hmm, none right now, might need to be added to the test logger. But something for future improvement.

> I'm thinking more like machine resource starvation from the parallel test runs.

I didn't know we ran works in parallel. Are you thinking about thread starvation here? I believe we run the server on a separate thread (at the very least)

We run everything in parallel I believe, so other test projects could be running, even builds and packs could be running at the same time I think.

I think I told Pranav once that you might see improved test reliability once Components moved to Helix because then you'll have a dedicated machine for just Components tests.

I haven't been able to find any of these tests in the `Quarantined Tests` view in WhatsBroken. Was thinking about unquarantining this.
These tests aren't running in Helix, so you can't use WhatsBroken to see if they are failing or not.
@BrennanConroy recently reported that nearly all of the tests in this type are currently quarantined. We should revisit this type to determine if there's a fundamental test / product issue.

Update on this. We placed some fixes for this issue in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/29056.

* `DispatchedEventsWillKeepBeingProcessed_ButUpdatedWillBeDelayedUntilARenderIsAcknowledged`
* `ComponentDisposeMethodThrowsExceptionTerminatesTheCircuit`

But not for others. :/

We should monitor this for another week then compare the first half of the 30-day analytics and the second-half to see what effect the changes above had.

`ComponentDisposeMethodThrowsExceptionTerminatesTheCircuit` has a 78% pass rate
`ComponentLifecycleMethodThrowsExceptionTerminatesTheCircuit` has a 4% pass rate (**this is our lowest passing rate test**)

Round #2: put another fix for this in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/32189.

For the DataProtection issue, you can try adding https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/a6c7f768ef10b8bce34f5db7c8a8594106efb8a5/src/SignalR/server/SignalR/test/Startup.cs#L69-L72 to avoid parallel test issues
What is this tracking, didn't you effectively remove this class and the tests are now a. unquarantined, b. very different?

I moved out some of the tests that were quarantined to a different infrastructure. If that infrastructure proves to be stable (aka none of them get quarantined), then we'll migrate the rest. We still have tests quarantined with this label (those are the ones that will need to be migrated).

Note these tests don't run on Helix and aspnetcore-quarantined-tests only runs Helix tests. See [analytics for aspnetcore-quarantined-pr](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/public/_test/analytics?definitionId=869&contextType=build) for these tests. To make things a bit more annoying, only individual test names show up in the analytics (they aren't qualified). Searching for a test in each quarantined class shows they are **not** doing well at all -- the best is running at about 46% success. Removing the test-fixed label…

Yep -- the "test-fixed" label was to indicate that action was taken on this.

The action we took and future work is written out in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/19666#issuecomment-859742472.
Closing, `ComponentHubReliabilityTest` no longer exists (I think tests were moved to different classes/re-written elsewhere).

review_comments: @BrennanConroy will this leave the hubconnection in an invalid state if the call fails?
It will leave it in a disconnected state
I'm explictly asking if re-using the same hubconnection for the retries is OK

Yes.

Although I'd love to know why you think this is needed. SignalR has 100's of tests that use the HubConnection to connect to a server and doesn't need to use retries.
I'm just being cautious here. Based on the error I have not much idea of what can be going wrong. Other than the server is taking longer to start?
